tauceti:Completed/ContourIntegration.summary: Everything this completed roadmap asks for is built, sorry-free, in Tau Ceti under TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/ (123 files, about 1150 declarations, no sorry or axiom). That covers: piecewise-C¹ curves, immersions and ℤ-cycles; the PV-defined generalized winding number with integrality, homotopy invariance and vanishing on the unbounded component; the model sector and HW Props 2.2 and 2.3; residues via meromorphicOrderAt, polar-part decompositions, the circle and null-homologous classical residue theorems and the argument principle; the homology Cauchy theorem and integral formula by Dixon's argument, for curves and cycles; and HW Thm 3.3 with conditions (A′)/(B), in single-curve and cycle forms, plus the half-residue case, a simple-pole unconditional form, real-axis PV applications and the Dirichlet integral. Mathlib contributes only ingredients (circle/disc/annulus/rectangle Cauchy theory, the circle Cauchy integral formula, curve integrals with C²-homotopy invariance, meromorphicOrderAt, logDeriv). It has no winding number, principal value, residue, principal-part/Laurent-coefficient API (the README wrongly credits Mathlib with principal-part machinery), residue theorem, argument principle or homology Cauchy theorem. Genuinely missing, and outside the pinned scope: HW Thm 3.3 for accumulation-free singular sets and essential singularities (the residue is only meaningful at meromorphic points), cycle-level versions of Props 2.2/2.3, a cyclic re-basing lemma to remove the basepoint-off-singularity hypotheses, and a signed-curvature API.

targets.target: Piecewise-C¹ curves on [a,b]: continuity, finitely many breakpoints, C¹ pieces, integrable/bounded derivative
targets.note: Predicate on a raw function γ : ℝ → ℂ over uIcc a b (continuity + a finite breakpoint set off which every closed subinterval is C¹), as the roadmap's function-based convention prescribes; no sorry in the file. Mathlib has no piecewise-C¹ curve notion (only ContDiffOn and C¹ paths).

targets.target: Closed piecewise-C¹ immersions (non-vanishing one-sided derivative on every piece, γ a = γ b)
targets.note: IsPwC1ImmersionOn requires derivWithin ≠ 0 on every closed breakpoint-free piece (one-sided at piece ends, including a and b); closedness γ a = γ b is kept as a separate theorem hypothesis, not bundled. No sorry.

targets.target: Cycles: finite formal ℤ-combinations of closed piecewise-C¹ curves, with additive integral/winding number/trace
targets.note: Cycle := FreeAbelianGroup PiecewiseC1ClosedCurve (a small bundle of an interval-restricted closed piecewise-C¹ curve); integral and winding number are the additive extensions (winding number is an AddMonoidHom Cycle →+ ℂ). No sorry.

targets.target: Interval-integrability of γ'·(f∘γ) for f continuous on the image
targets.note: Tau Ceti: vector-valued f continuous on γ '' [[a,b]], γ piecewise C¹. Mathlib only has curve-integrability of a continuous 1-form along a C¹ Path (no breakpoints).

targets.target: Generalized winding number n_{z₀}(C) = PV (2πi)⁻¹ ∮ dz/(z−z₀) (HW Def 2.1), defined for every z₀ including z₀ on C, with the Cauchy-PV predicate kept separate from integrability
targets.note: windingNumber γ a b z₀ = (2πi)⁻¹·cauchyPVAt γ a b (· − z₀)⁻¹ z₀, a limUnder value (junk if the PV does not exist); HasCauchyPVAt carries an eventual-integrability clause plus the ε→0⁺ limit of the symmetric-excision integrals. Mathlib has no winding number and no principal value.

targets.target: Classical case z₀ ∉ C: the PV is the ordinary index integral
targets.note: Hypotheses: γ continuous on uIcc a b, avoids z₀, index integrand interval-integrable (cycle form: z ∉ trace C). No sorry.

targets.target: Integrality n_{z₀}(C) ∈ ℤ off the curve, via the exp-primitive argument
targets.note: exp(2πi·n) = (γ b − w)/(γ a − w) for any avoiding arc (continuous, differentiable off a countable set), so closedness gives n ∈ ℤ; piecewise-C¹ and cycle forms included. Mathlib only has the circle computation circleIntegral.integral_sub_inv_of_mem_ball.

targets.target: Homotopy invariance of the winding number in ℂ ∖ C (point moving in a component; curve deformed through ℂ ∖ {z₀})
targets.note: Tau Ceti: invariance under an arbitrary continuous fixed-endpoint Path.Homotopy avoiding w (end paths piecewise C¹ on [0,1]); free (unbased) loop homotopies are not stated separately. Constancy on components of ℂ ∖ image for curves and cycles. Mathlib only has equality of curve integrals of closed 1-forms under a C² homotopy (no winding number).

targets.target: n_{z₀}(C) = 0 on the unbounded component of ℂ ∖ C
targets.note: Stated for any unbounded component of the complement (closed curve, piecewise C¹ or raw regularity; also for cycles). No sorry.

targets.target: Model sector (HW (2.4)): corner curve of two radii and an arc of opening α has n₀ = α/2π
targets.note: windingNumber (modelSector z₀ r φ α) (−r) (r+α) z₀ = α/2π for 0 < r, 0 ≤ α (the corner reading needs 0 < α < 2π, where it also equals crossingAngle/2π). Proved as a genuine principal value at the corner. No sorry.

targets.target: Seeded values: winding ½ at a smooth boundary point (semicircle, α = π) and 1/6 at a π/3 corner
targets.note: Model-sector ½ and 1/6 values, plus the bare arc index integrals over [0,π] and [0,π/3]. The on-contour values at ρ, ρ+1 for the actual fundamental-domain boundary live in the ModularForms consumer (sorry-free), outside this roadmap.

targets.target: HW Prop 2.2 (finiteness): a closed piecewise-C¹ immersion meets any point only finitely often
targets.note: (uIcc a b ∩ γ⁻¹{z₀}).Finite for any IsPwC1ImmersionOn curve (closedness not needed); crossings are isolated by the non-vanishing one-sided tangents. No sorry.

targets.target: HW Prop 2.2 (winding decomposition): n_{z₀}(Λ) = n_{z₀}(Λ̃) + Σ_ℓ α_ℓ/2π with Λ̃ avoiding z₀
targets.note: Hypotheses: IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b, a < b, γ a = γ b, and basepoint γ a ≠ s (a WLOG normalisation for a closed curve, but no cyclic re-basing lemma is provided). Λ̃ is the explicit circular-cap excision exciseCrossings γ s windows (closed, piecewise C¹, avoiding s); the angles are crossingAngle γ t over the canonical finite crossing set. The identity is at the level of winding numbers, for one curve (no cycle-level version).

targets.target: HW Prop 2.3: for a closed piecewise-C^{1,1} immersion, n₀(Λ) = (1/2π)∫(xẏ − yẋ)/(x²+y²) dt with bounded integrand (no PV)
targets.note: Needs IsPwC1ImmersionOn, closedness, basepoint γ a ≠ s, and only one-sided C^{1,1} (Lipschitz derivWithin) at each crossing, not global C^{1,1}; boundedness and integrability of the real integrand are proved, not assumed. The integrand realWindingIntegrand z v := (z⁻¹·v).im is defined at TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Winding/Integrand.lean:31 (missing from the tsv because of its `public noncomputable def` prefix). No sorry.

targets.target: Crossing value: the real integrand tends to ½·k_Λ·|Λ̇| = (ẋÿ − ẏẍ)/(2(ẋ²+ẏ²)) at a crossing (C² near t̃)
targets.note: ContDiffAt ℝ 2 γ t₀ with deriv γ t₀ ≠ 0 gives the explicit limit on 𝓝[≠] t₀; a variant needs only differentiability near t₀ and a derivative of deriv γ at t₀. Stated in explicit coordinates, as the roadmap asks (neither library has a signed-curvature API). No sorry.

targets.target: Relate the complex PV form and the real form of the winding number
targets.note: Im of any PV of (z−w)⁻¹ along γ equals the ordinary integral of the real integrand whenever the latter is interval-integrable; the curve may pass through w. No sorry.

targets.target: FTC along an arc: F' = f along the image of γ ⇒ ∮_γ f = F(γ b) − F(γ a); hence 0 for a closed curve
targets.note: Tau Ceti asks HasDerivAt G (g (γ t)) (γ t) only at parameters in the open interval, plus continuity of G∘γ and integrability (weaker than a neighbourhood of the image). Mathlib has the real FTC and the circle case only.

targets.target: Cauchy's theorem for a contractible contour, reconciled with Mathlib's disc statements
targets.note: Tau Ceti: a piecewise-C¹ loop with a continuous Path.Homotopy to the constant path inside open Ω integrates holomorphic f to 0; also any closed piecewise-C¹ curve in a star-shaped open set or disc. Obtained from the Layer-3 homology theorem rather than from the arc FTC. Mathlib only has circles/rectangles/annuli and primitives on discs (simply connected domains are a TODO in HasPrimitives).

targets.target: Residue Res_{z₀} f as the order-(−1) Laurent coefficient, built on meromorphicOrderAt
targets.note: Defined for f meromorphic at z₀ (0 at non-poles, junk 0 where f is not meromorphic), so residues at essential isolated singularities are not covered; this matches the roadmap's own convention of building the residue on meromorphicOrderAt. Mathlib has no residue, Laurent coefficients or principal parts (only order, normal form and trailing coefficient).

targets.target: Simple-pole value Res_{z₀} f = lim_{z→z₀} (z − z₀) f(z)
targets.note: Both directions: at order −1 the product converges to the residue, and if f is meromorphic and the product converges to L then residue = L. No sorry.

targets.target: ℂ-linearity of the residue
targets.note: Additivity requires MeromorphicAt of the summands (necessarily); scaling is unconditional. No sorry.

targets.target: Simple-pole decomposition f = (holomorphic) + Σ_s Res_s f/(z − s) (and the general polar-part decomposition)
targets.note: Open U, finite S, f differentiable on U ∖ S, meromorphic with order ≥ −1 at each s ∈ S: a g differentiable on all of U with f = g + Σ Res_s f/(z−s) on U ∖ S. The higher-order version (finite Laurent tails) is ofMeromorphic. No sorry.

targets.target: Classical residue theorem, disc/circle case: ∮_{C(c,R)} f = 2πi Σ_s Res_s f with the finite pole set inside
targets.note: f meromorphic on the closed disc (R > 0), all poles in a finite S ⊆ open disc; raw f may differ from its meromorphic normal form at isolated points. The two-simple-pole acceptance example is included. No sorry.

targets.target: Recovering the Cauchy integral formula
targets.note: Mathlib already has the circle Cauchy integral formula. Tau Ceti computes Res_{z₀}(g/(z−z₀)^{k+1}) = g^{(k)}(z₀)/k! and derives the winding-weighted formula for any closed curve in a disc or null-homologous in U; no Tau Ceti lemma re-derives the circle formula itself from classicalResidueTheorem_circle, which is not needed.

targets.target: General arbitrary-cycle classical residue theorem ∮_C f = 2πi Σ_s n_s(C) Res_s f for a null-homologous C avoiding S (layer defers it to Layer 3+)
targets.note: Open U, finite S, f differentiable on U ∖ S and meromorphic at points of S in U, a closed piecewise-C¹ curve (or cycle) in U avoiding S and null-homologous in U. Proved via the polar decomposition plus the homology Cauchy theorem. No sorry.

targets.target: Res_z(f'/f) = ord_z f
targets.note: f meromorphic at z₀ with meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = n ∈ ℤ gives residue (logDeriv f) z₀ = n. Mathlib has only AnalyticAt.tendsto_mul_logDeriv_simple_zero (simple zeros). No sorry.

targets.target: Argument principle (2πi)⁻¹ ∮_C f'/f = Σ_z ord_z f (zeros minus poles, with multiplicity)
targets.note: Circle form (f meromorphic on the closed disc, nonzero-order points in a finite S inside), a form using Mathlib's MeromorphicOn.divisor, and a winding-weighted form for null-homologous curves avoiding S. The on-contour version is in Layer 4. Mathlib has logDeriv and meromorphicOrderAt but not this identity.

targets.target: Homology Cauchy theorem: f holomorphic on open Ω, C a cycle in Ω null-homologous in Ω ⇒ ∮_C f = 0
targets.note: Single closed piecewise-C¹ curve and genuine ℤ-cycles, with null-homology imposed on the whole cycle (cancellation between generators allowed). Mathlib has only disc/annulus/rectangle Cauchy theorems. No sorry.

targets.target: Homology form of the Cauchy integral formula f(z)·n_z(C) = (2πi)⁻¹ ∮_C f(w)/(w − z) dw
targets.note: For z ∈ U off the curve/trace; also all iterated derivatives (weight f^{(k)}(z)/k!), for curves and cycles. No sorry.

targets.target: Subsumes the null-homotopic case (null-homotopic ⇒ null-homologous)
targets.note: A piecewise-C¹ loop with a continuous Path.Homotopy to the constant path inside Ω is null-homologous in Ω (one direction only). No sorry.

targets.target: Dixon's argument: g(w,z) = (f(w)−f(z))/(w−z) glues to an entire function that vanishes by Liouville
targets.note: dixonH1/dixonH2/dixonFunction are irreducible_def definitions (no axioms); the glued function is entire and tends to 0 at infinity, hence 0. The theorem is named the homology Cauchy theorem and Dixon's proof is attributed, as the layer asks. No sorry.

targets.target: HW Thm 3.3 (pinned form): U open, S ⊆ U finite, f holomorphic on U ∖ S and meromorphic on S, C a null-homologous closed piecewise-C¹ immersion in U (basepoint off S) ⇒ PV (2πi)⁻¹∮_C f = Σ_s n_s(C) Res_s f
targets.note: Conclusion HasCauchyPV γ a b f (2πi·Σ_{s∈S} n_s(γ)·Res_s f) under (A′) and (B) plus the listed hypotheses; the cycle version asks immersion, basepoint and (A′)/(B) of each generator. HasCauchyPV excises ε-balls about some finite set (existentially bound; value unique). The paper's accumulation-free S and locally straight essential singularities remain out of scope, as the layer's pinned form says. No sorry.

targets.target: Subsumption: classical residue theorem (poles off C) and the half-residue case (on-cycle simple pole with winding ½ contributes πi·Res_s f)
targets.note: The half-residue theorem assumes windingNumber γ a b s = 1/2; the simple-pole form discharges (A′) and (B). The concrete PV of dz/z along the half-disc boundary is πi. The off-curve case is stated separately and needs no immersion. No sorry.

targets.target: Regularity conditions (A′) (finite crossings, flatness matching the pole order) and (B) (sector-cancellation compatibility of higher-order Laurent parts), stated explicitly
targets.note: (A′): each s ∈ S is met finitely often, and at an interior or basepoint crossing of a pole of order n the curve is flat of order n (HW Def 3.2, perpendicular distance to a one-sided tangent line). (B): at every order > 1 on-curve pole the crossing (or basepoint) angle is a rational multiple of π, and k·θ ∈ 2πℤ for each nonzero higher Laurent coefficient. Both are Prop-valued structures; they are hypotheses, not sorry. No sorry in the file.

targets.target: Higher-order poles: simple-pole case first, then the general meromorphic case via the Laurent principal part and sector cancellation under (B)
targets.note: At worst simple poles, (A′) and (B) are automatic, so that regime needs no conditions. For order k ≥ 2 the PV of c/(z−s)^k along a flat, sector-compatible immersion is the endpoint difference of the antiderivative, hence 0 on a closed curve. The general theorem runs through PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic. No sorry.

targets.target: Application: improper integrals and Cauchy principal values along the real axis that the classical theorem cannot reach
targets.note: PV along [−R, R] with a simple pole at 0 and simple poles in the upper half-disc; PV of e^{iaz}/z along [−R, R] → πi; the Dirichlet integral ∫₀^R sin x/x → π/2 (Mathlib has Real.sinc but not this value); Jordan's lemma. The half-disc construction pins the real-axis singularity at the origin. No sorry.

targets.target: Application: the valence formula's treatment of the on-contour points i and ρ
targets.note: The engine is an argument principle for a null-homologous closed immersion running through the zeros and poles (PV of f'/f = 2πi Σ n_z(γ) ord_z f, basepoint off S). The level-one valence formula ord_∞ + ½ord_i + ⅓ord_ρ + Σ ord_q = k/12 is proved sorry-free in the ModularForms consumer (whole LevelOne directory has no sorry).
